I want to use Covariate analysis (I know that I have heterogeneous cells in cancer tissue samples but I have no information about them) and in this case the number of DMR are very low (29 on the promoter region) in comparison to default Diffmeth analysis (2409 on the promoter region). Should I continue with counting for Covariates to not having many false positives and in this case should I simulate my data in advance?

Kind Regards,

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] applying covariates and simulation of methylation data
parts:
there is no covariate argument in your calculateDiffMeth() functions, you are not accounting for anything. Maybe you are mixing concepts. 
You are using two different tests, one of them is the default one the other one does over-dispersion correction. I think with overdispersion correction you will have less false positives even though it gives fewer DMRs. 

Best,
Altuna
